title: A Vaccine for One of the World's Biggest Child Killers
hook: Diarrheal disease kills over a million people a year, nearly half of them children under five. A vaccine against shigella — a leading cause — is now in trials.
key_points: More than 1 million people die of diarrheal disease each year worldwide.
Nearly half of those deaths are children under the age of five.
Shigella is a major bacterial cause, spread through contaminated food, water, and hands.
A vaccine candidate now in clinical trials is the most promising prevention tool yet.
There is currently no licensed shigella vaccine anywhere in the world.
content_html: Diarrheal disease sounds mundane in a country with clean water and easy rehydration. Globally it is a mass killer: more than a million deaths a year, and nearly half of them children under five.
extra_html:
As NPR reports, a vaccine candidate targeting shigella — one of the leading bacterial causes — has moved into clinical trials, and researchers describe it as the most hopeful prevention tool the field has had. Shigella spreads through contaminated food and water and unwashed hands, and it thrives exactly where sanitation is weakest, which is also where children are least able to survive a severe bout of dehydration.

There is currently no licensed shigella vaccine anywhere. Trial results still have to arrive before anyone can promise anything, but the target is unusually well chosen: a single, common pathogen behind a huge share of preventable childhood death.

related.title: Vaccines Adults Still Need
related.hook: Vaccination isn't just a childhood checklist. Protection from some shots fades, new ones are recommended with age, and a few need regular boosters.

related.title: Handwashing: The Cheapest Medicine
related.hook: It sounds almost too simple, but washing your hands well is one of the most effective things you can do to stop the spread of illness in a household.

flashcards.prompt: Why is a shigella vaccine considered such a big deal?
flashcards.back_html: Diarrheal disease kills more than a million people a year, and nearly half are children under five. Shigella is one of the leading bacterial causes, and there is no licensed vaccine against it yet.

flashcards.prompt: Roughly what share of annual diarrheal-disease deaths are in children under five?

choices.text: Almost none — it mainly kills older adults

flashcards.explanation_html: Of the more than 1 million people who die of diarrheal disease each year, nearly half are children under the age of five — which is why prevention aimed at this group carries so much weight.
